---
title: "3. Blood data with bloodstream"
---

[bloodstream](https://github.com/mathesong/bloodstream) models arterial blood data and produces an arterial input function for each PET scan. You choose a model for each blood component in an app, and bloodstream fits the models and writes a report.

You will run bloodstream twice. First with the default settings, and then you will fit models that you choose yourself.

## Start the app

Start bloodstream with the course script:

```bash
/neurodesktop-storage/course-material/pet/scripts/run_bloodstream.sh
```

The script finds a free port for the app, and prints the command that it runs and the link to the app. The command is:

```bash
apptainer run -B /neurodesktop-storage/course-material/pet/data/ds004869:/data:ro \
  /neurodesktop-storage/course-material/pet/containers/bloodstream.sif \
  --mode interactive --bids_dir /data --derivatives_dir ~/pet_course/derivatives
```

What the command does:

- `apptainer run ... bloodstream.sif` runs the bloodstream container.
- `-B ...ds004869:/data:ro` makes the dataset visible inside the container as `/data`, read-only.
- `--bids_dir /data` tells bloodstream where the BIDS data are.
- `--derivatives_dir ~/pet_course/derivatives` tells bloodstream where to write its results: your own folder.

You can ignore these messages:

- `INFO: Environment variable SINGULARITYENV_MATLABPATH is set...`
- `WARNING: While bind mounting '/data:/data': destination is already in the mount point list`

## Open the app

Wait until the terminal shows `Listening on`. Then open the link that the script printed in a new browser tab.

## Run a default analysis

1. Restrict the analysis to the six workshop participants: `02;05;08;11;13;14`.
2. Leave all the other settings as they are, and run the pipeline from the app. Keep the app's tab open until the app closes itself.

The run takes several minutes, and its progress appears in the terminal.

The results are in `~/pet_course/derivatives/bloodstream/Primary_Analysis`. To open the report, run:

```bash
/neurodesktop-storage/course-material/pet/scripts/view_bloodstream.sh
```

The script prints a link. Open it in a new browser tab. When you are done, press Ctrl+C in the terminal.

::: {.callout-tip}
## Open reports on the Desktop

You can also open the bloodstream reports in the web browser on the Neurodesk **Desktop**, without the script. On the Desktop, you can also look through all the output files that bloodstream wrote, in `~/pet_course/derivatives/bloodstream`.
:::

- What did the default settings do with each blood component?
- Do the curves look reasonable for every participant?
- Do any measurements look a little bit off?

## Fit models to the data

Start the app again, this time with the `--analysis_foldername` option, so that the new results go to a separate folder and don't replace the default analysis:

```bash
/neurodesktop-storage/course-material/pet/scripts/run_bloodstream.sh --analysis_foldername Modelled
```

The script passes any options that you add on to bloodstream.

1. Open the link that the script prints, as before.
2. Restrict the analysis to the six workshop participants: `02;05;08;11;13;14`.
3. Choose a model for the parent fraction, the blood-to-plasma ratio, and the arterial input function (splines are quickest). What do the options mean, and which would you choose for each?
4. Run the pipeline, and keep the tab open until the app closes itself.

The results are in `~/pet_course/derivatives/bloodstream/Modelled`. To open the report, run the view script with the name of the analysis folder:

```bash
/neurodesktop-storage/course-material/pet/scripts/view_bloodstream.sh Modelled
```

- Do the model fits look reasonable for every participant?
- How do the results differ from the default analysis?
